name: Orbital Industries (formerly Orbital Materials)
subcategory: AI materials discovery -> 'AI Industrial' (CurieOS platform, data-centre cooling hardware)
origin_detail: London-datelined company (BASF ECMS release, 5 Aug 2026), formerly Orbital Materials. orbitalmaterials.com now 301-redirects to orbitalindustries.com and the GitHub organization is still 'orbital-materials'. Backers shown on its site: Plural, NVentures (NVIDIA), Radical Ventures, Compound, Fly Ventures. Founders and founding year were not confirmed in fetched sources.
flagship_projects: Orb universal interatomic potentials: v1 (Sep 2024), v2 (Oct 2024), v3 (Apr 2025), OrbMol (Aug 2025), OrbMol-v2 (May 2026); Apache-2.0
CurieOS agentic AI platform for science and engineering (11 Aug 2026)
Orbital IT two-phase direct-to-chip GPU cooling (PFAS-free fluid)
openness_notes: Its foundation models are open. orb-models (code and weights) is Apache-2.0 on GitHub (~630 stars, ~94 forks), with no commercial-use restrictions stated. OrbMol was trained on Open Molecules 2025 (OMol25, '100M+ high-accuracy DFT calculations') and OrbMol-v2 on OMol25 + OPoly26. The commercial products (CurieOS platform, cooling hardware, licensed discovery for BASF) are proprietary, and the company's boilerplate says every product is invented with its 'proprietary AI platform'. Open core: level 2.

license_history.license: CurieOS proprietary (licensed to BASF ECMS); Orb models still Apache-2.0

risk_events: By Nov 2026: renamed Orbital Industries and repositioned from materials discovery to an 'AI Industrial' building physical products (rename date not found)
Aug 2026: launched CurieOS; first product built with it is GPU cooling hardware (Orbital IT), i.e. a pivot toward data-centre infrastructure
5 Aug 2026: BASF Environmental Catalyst and Metal Solutions licensed CurieOS for automotive-emissions catalyst discovery (terms undisclosed)
robustness: The open Orb models are widely forked and Apache-licensed, so they would outlive the company. The business itself is a VC-backed, single-company proprietary platform that has pivoted toward data-centre hardware. Funding size and runway are unknown.
physical_science_relevance: Very high. Its open universal interatomic potentials (Orb, OrbMol) are used for atomistic simulation of crystals, molecules and polymers. It does catalyst discovery for automotive emissions (BASF ECMS) and invented a PFAS-free heat-transfer material for GPU cooling.
openness_effect_assessment: Orbital is this group's clearest example of an AI-for-materials startup releasing permissive open weights. Its models were trained partly on open public datasets (OMol25), and the releases built scientific credibility and adoption (~630 stars, ~94 forks). Monetization moved to proprietary layers (CurieOS licences, cooling hardware): an open-model, closed-product split. The 2026 pivot to data-centre cooling shows the open models alone were not the business.
key_takeaway: Orbital (Materials, now Industries) shows that an AI-for-materials startup can stay genuinely open at the model layer: Apache-2.0 Orb potentials trained on open DFT datasets such as OMol25. It still has to find revenue in closed products, here an agentic R&D platform licensed to BASF and PFAS-free GPU cooling for AI data centres. Openness bought reputation and community, not revenue, and the company's rebrand to an 'AI Industrial' signals where it expects the money.
